brief.headline: Push for a 5–8% price cut — they earn 5.9% net margin vs 3.8% peer median and have room to give

priceAsk.summary: Request a 5–8% reduction on rigid plastic packaging rates
priceAsk.target: A cut that narrows the gap to their peer median net margin of 3.8%
priceAsk.basis: Chemco runs a 5.9% net margin — 210 basis points above the 3.8% peer median — demonstrating pricing headroom. HDPE resin import unit value sits at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a market benchmark to anchor the conversation.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at current 30 Days After Receipt, but use it as a trade: offer faster payment only in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Maintaining 30 days protects ₹45.14 L in working capital; moving to 15 days would free an additional ₹22.57 L, but only if we extract equivalent price savings

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco is financially solid — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, 16.1% EBITDA margin, 16.3% return on capital (vs 14.9% peer median), and 2.94x interest coverage. Debt-to-equity of 0.83x is manageable. Our ₹5.49 Cr spend is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue, so we're not a make-or-break account. However, their 104d cash conversion cycle vs 79d peer median and 49d payable days vs 37d peer median show they squeeze their own suppliers and tie up cash longer than peers — they value liquidity and speed, which gives us a lever. Their 5.9% net margin vs 3.8% peer median is our strongest card: they can afford to discount without financial distress.

evidence.point: Chemco earns a 5.9% net margin, 210 basis points above the 3.8% peer median
They stretch supplier payables to 49 days, 12 days longer than the 37-day peer median
Their cash conversion cycle is 104 days vs a 79-day peer median, tying up working capital 25 days longer
HDPE resin import unit value provides a market-line anchor
Our annual spend is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue
Solid credit rating reduces continuity risk

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate and already a second source for us on packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable (Health: A) — a robust alternate for bottles/closures and already a second source for packaging.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded & blow-moulded packaging supplier with broad capability across bottles/caps.

risks: Our ₹5.49 Cr is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — we lack volume leverage, so frame the ask around fairness (peer margins, market resin price) rather than threat of exit.
Their CRISIL A+ / Stable rating and 2.94x interest coverage mean they won't buckle under pressure — avoid overplaying our hand.
Probe42 financial score is 4/10 despite strong ratios; confirm no hidden risks (working-capital stress, covenant breaches) before pushing hard.
They already pay suppliers at 49d vs 37d peer median — asking for extended terms may meet resistance unless we offer a quid pro quo (volume, longer contract).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've benchmarked your 5.9% net margin against the 3.8% peer median and HDPE resin at 87.61 ₹/kg — let's discuss how we can align our pricing to reflect those fundamentals and deepen our partnership.
